page: Microsoft Azure D2ls_v6 is an entry-level virtual machine within the Dlsv6 series, configured with 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core across two hardware threads. The instance runs on an Intel Xeon 8573B processor clocked up to 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, supported by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions). System memory is allocated at 4.0 GB total, yielding a reduced 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The virtual machine includes no bundled local ephemeral storage and allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, operating under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-threaded execution offset by lower overall parallel capacity due to its two-thread limit. In Geekbench testing, the instance achieved a strong single-core score of 2134.0, complemented by high-throughput single-threaded gzip compression at 31.36 GB/sec. However, multi-core throughput is constrained, registering a Geekbench multi-core score of 2620.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 3771.93. Memory bandwidth testing shows 20.87 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 14.17 GB/sec for uncached writes, placing large-block memory streaming in the lower quartile of tested cloud environments.

From an operational cost perspective, the instance provides an economical entry point for applications requiring modern architectural extensions without paying for excess RAM capacity. The 1:2 core-to-memory ratio provides efficiency for CPU-focused microservices, lightweight API proxies, and basic background workers. The architectural tradeoff centers on the total memory ceiling and the complete absence of local disk, requiring remote storage solutions for persistent data needs.

The hardware configuration is suited for low-footprint compute services, small-scale web serving, linting, light CI/CD test runners, and single-stream data formatting tasks. Workloads involving larger in-memory datasets, parallelized compilation, or database operations will be bottlenecked by the 4.0 GB memory capacity and dual-thread execution footprint.
description: Microsoft Azure D2ls_v6 is a compute-focused general-purpose virtual machine designed for lean workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573B processor operating at 4.2 GHz, the instance supplies 2 vCPUs across 1 physical core, 4.0 GB of system memory, and advanced instruction sets including Intel AMX and AVX-512. The instance contains no bundled local storage, relying on external network-attached disks for storage operations. Benchmark evaluations show strong single-core compute performance, as reflected in high Geekbench single-core and gzip compression results, balanced against modest multi-core capacity and lower memory bandwidth. With its 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the D2ls_v6 represents a cost-efficient deployment profile for single-threaded processing, lightweight web serving, continuous integration runners, and small utility microservices.
